title: Direct object pronouns: lo, la, los, las
summary: Stop repeating nouns: ¿El pan? Lo compro yo. ¿La tarta? La hace mi madre.
focus: Direct object pronouns me, te, lo, la, nos, os, los, las, their position, and the personal a
content:
## The direct object and the personal a

The **direct object** is the person or thing that receives the action. Find it by asking *¿qué?* or *¿a quién?* after the verb.

- *Compro el pan.* (¿Qué compro? El pan.)
- *Veo a María.* (¿A quién veo? A María.)

When the direct object is a **specific person** (or a pet), Spanish puts the **personal a** in front of it. It has no English translation.

- *Espero a Juan.* (I'm waiting for Juan, but *Espero el autobús.*)
- *Llamo a mis padres.* (I call my parents.)
- *Conozco a tu hermana.* (I know your sister.)

## The pronouns

Once the listener knows what you are talking about, you can replace the noun with a pronoun.

| | singular | plural |
|---|---|---|
| 1st person | **me** (me) | **nos** (us) |
| 2nd person | **te** (you) | **os** (you all) |
| 3rd person masc. | **lo** (him, it, you *usted*) | **los** (them) |
| 3rd person fem. | **la** (her, it, you *usted*) | **las** (them) |

**Lo / la / los / las** copy the gender and number of the noun they replace.

- *¿El pan? Lo compro yo.* (The bread? I'll buy it.)
- *¿La tarta? La hace mi madre.* (The cake? My mother makes it.)
- *¿Las gafas? Las tengo en la mochila.* (The glasses? I have them in my backpack.)

## Where the pronoun goes

With one **conjugated verb**, the pronoun goes **in front of it**, and *no* goes in front of the pronoun.

- *Te llamo mañana.* (I'll call you tomorrow.)
- *No lo encuentro.* (I can't find it.)

With an **infinitive** or a **gerund** you have two correct options. Put the pronoun before the conjugated verb, or **attach** it to the infinitive or gerund (the gerund then needs an accent).

- *Quiero verlo.* = *Lo quiero ver.* (I want to see it.)
- *Estoy leyéndola.* = *La estoy leyendo.* (I'm reading it.)
- *Voy a comprarlas.* = *Las voy a comprar.* (I'm going to buy them.)

Affirmative commands also attach the pronoun: *¡Cómpralo!* (see the imperative lesson).

## Lo or le? A note on leísmo

**Lo** and **la** are the direct object pronouns, including for *usted*: *Señor García, lo llamo mañana.*

In much of Spain people say **le** instead of **lo** when the direct object is a **man or boy**: *A Juan le veo todos los días.* This is **leísmo**, and the Academy accepts it only for a singular male person. You will hear it and may use it, but **lo** is correct everywhere. *Le* for a thing (*le compro* for *el pan*) or for a woman is always wrong.

vocabulary.example_meaning: They're inviting us to the wedding.
Will you wait for me at the door?
Shall I help you with the bags?

vocabulary.example: A mis abuelos los visito los domingos.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I visit my grandparents on Sundays.

vocabulary.example: No encuentro las llaves. ¿Las has visto?
vocabulary.example_meaning: I can't find the keys. Have you seen them?
The present? We'll buy it together.

vocabulary.example: ¿Dónde está mi móvil? No lo encuentro.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Where's my mobile? I can't find it.

vocabulary.example: Las gafas las tengo en la mochila.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The glasses, I've got them in my backpack.
The cake? My mother makes it.

vocabulary.example: Estoy leyéndola; es una novela muy buena.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I'm reading it; it's a very good novel.

quiz.explanation: 'El pan' is masculine singular, so 'lo'. 'Le' is never used for a thing.
hints: What gender and number is 'el pan'?

quiz.prompt: Replace the object with a pronoun: Mi madre hace la tarta. → Mi madre ___ hace.
quiz.explanation: 'La tarta' is feminine singular, so the pronoun is 'la': 'Mi madre la hace.'
hints: The pronoun goes in front of the verb.

quiz.prompt: ¿Visitas a tus abuelos? — Sí, ___ visito los domingos.
quiz.explanation: 'Tus abuelos' is masculine plural, so the pronoun is 'los'. The personal 'a' disappears when the pronoun replaces the noun. 'Les' for a plural direct object is not accepted.
hints: Leísmo is only tolerated in the masculine singular.

quiz.prompt: Complete with the pronoun: ¿Dónde está mi móvil? No ___ encuentro.
quiz.explanation: 'Mi móvil' is masculine singular, so the pronoun is 'lo', placed between 'no' and the verb: 'No lo encuentro.'
hints: Put the pronoun between no and the verb.

quiz.prompt: Where does me go? Pick the correct question.
quiz.explanation: With a single conjugated verb the pronoun goes in front: 'Me ayudas'. Pronouns only attach to infinitives, gerunds and affirmative commands.
hints: 'Ayudas' is a conjugated verb, not an infinitive.

quiz.prompt: Rewrite attaching the pronoun to the infinitive: Quiero leer la novela. → Quiero ___.
quiz.explanation: 'La novela' becomes 'la', attached to the end of the infinitive: 'Quiero leerla.' 'La quiero leer' is equally correct, but here the pronoun had to be attached.
hints: Write the infinitive and pronoun as one word.

quiz.explanation: 'Las gafas' is feminine plural → 'las': 'Las llevo en la mochila.'

quiz.prompt: Write the missing word: Esperamos ___ Juan en la estación.
quiz.explanation: Juan is a specific person and the direct object of esperar, so he takes the personal 'a': 'Esperamos a Juan.' (But 'Esperamos el tren.')
hints: A specific person as a direct object takes the personal a.

quiz.prompt: Which pair is correct and means the same thing?
options: Lo estoy leyendo. = Estoy lo leyendo.
quiz.explanation: With a gerund the pronoun either goes before the conjugated verb (estoy) or attaches to the gerund, which then needs an accent: 'leyéndolo'. It can never sit between the two verbs.
hints: Before the first verb, or glued to the gerund.
A pronoun attached to a gerund needs a written accent.

listening.meaning: Are you inviting us to your birthday?
listening.note: New word: el cumpleaños = the birthday.

listening.text: El regalo lo compro yo mañana.
listening.meaning: The present, I'll buy it tomorrow.
listening.note: The object named at the front is repeated as a pronoun.

listening.text: Las gafas las llevo siempre en el bolso.
listening.meaning: I always carry my glasses in my handbag.
listening.note: New word: el bolso = the handbag.

listening.text: Espero a Luis en la puerta del cine.
listening.meaning: I'm waiting for Luis at the cinema door.
listening.note: A specific person as direct object takes the personal a.

listening.text: La tarta de chocolate la hace mi abuela los domingos.
listening.meaning: My grandmother makes the chocolate cake on Sundays.

listening.text: ¿Dónde está mi móvil? Lo he dejado en la cocina.
listening.meaning: Where is my phone? I've left it in the kitchen.

listening.text: Quiero leer esta novela este verano, pero no la encuentro en casa.
listening.meaning: I want to read this novel this summer, but I can't find it at home.

guide.section: The direct object and the personal a

guide.tip: If you are unsure, say the full noun first, then swap it. ¿La tarta? Use la. ¿Los regalos? Use los. The pronoun always copies the noun.

conversations.title: The surprise party
conversations.scenario: Sara and Tomás are getting everything ready for their friend Laura's surprise birthday party.

lines.speaker: a
lines.meaning: Tomás, do you have Laura's present?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Sí, lo tengo en la mochila. ¿Y la tarta?
lines.meaning: Yes, I have it in my backpack. And the cake?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: La hace mi madre. La traemos esta tarde.
lines.meaning: My mother is making it. We're bringing it this afternoon.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Perfecto. ¿Has invitado a sus compañeros de trabajo?
lines.meaning: Perfect. Have you invited her workmates?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Sí, los he invitado a todos. ¿Me ayudas con las bebidas?
lines.meaning: Yes, I've invited them all. Will you help me with the drinks?
lines.note: los stands for sus compañeros, and me stands for the speaker

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Claro, te ayudo. Las compramos en el súper de la esquina.
lines.meaning: Of course, I'll help you. We'll buy them at the shop on the corner.
lines.note: te stands for you, and las stands for las bebidas

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¿Y las gafas de sol para la foto? No las encuentro.
lines.meaning: And the sunglasses for the photo? I can't find them.
lines.note: The order is no, then las, then the verb.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Están en el coche. Voy a buscarlas ahora.
lines.meaning: They're in the car. I'll go and get them now.
lines.note: The pronoun is attached to the infinitive.

lines.speaker: a
lines.meaning: What time does Laura arrive? Shall I call her?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: No, no la llames. ¡Es una sorpresa! Yo la espero en la puerta.
lines.meaning: No, don't call her. It's a surprise! I'll wait for her at the door.
lines.note: esperar a Laura becomes la espero

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Vale. ¡Qué nervios! Los invitados ya nos esperan.
lines.meaning: OK. I'm so nervous! The guests are already waiting for us.

bites.title: Who or what gets the action
bites.rule: The direct object answers ¿qué? or ¿a quién? after the verb. A specific person as direct object takes the personal a, as in Veo a María. A thing does not, as in Veo la tele.
bites.example: Espero a Juan. Espero el autobús.
bites.example_meaning: I'm waiting for Juan. I'm waiting for the bus.

bites.title: Eight small words
bites.rule: The pronouns are me, te, lo / la, nos, os and los / las. Lo, la, los and las copy the gender and number of the noun they replace.
bites.example_meaning: The cake? My mother makes it.

bites.title: In front of the verb
bites.rule: The pronoun goes before a conjugated verb, and no goes before the pronoun, as in No lo veo. Never put the pronoun after a conjugated verb.
bites.example: Te llamo mañana. No lo encuentro.
bites.example_meaning: I'll call you tomorrow. I can't find it.

bites.title: Attached to the infinitive
bites.rule: With an infinitive or gerund you can choose: Quiero verlo or Lo quiero ver, Estoy leyéndola or La estoy leyendo. A pronoun attached to a gerund adds an accent.
bites.example: Voy a comprarlas. = Las voy a comprar.

sorts.title: Which pronoun replaces it?
sorts.why: The pronoun copies the gender and number of the noun: el takes lo, la takes la, los takes los and las takes las.

sorts.title: Personal a or not?
sorts.why: A specific person as direct object takes the personal a; things do not.

sorts.title: Right place or wrong place?
sorts.why: The pronoun goes before the conjugated verb or attaches to the infinitive. It never goes after a conjugated verb or between the two verbs.

spots.why: Las llaves is feminine plural: las.

spots.sentence: ¿Nos esperas en la puerta? — Sí, les espero.
spots.why: Waiting for you all (vosotros) takes os, and les is not a direct object pronoun.
A pronoun attached to a gerund needs a written accent to keep the stress: leyéndola.

spots.sentence: ¿A tus abuelos? Les visito los domingos.
spots.why: Leísmo is only tolerated for one male person. A plural direct object takes los.
El regalo is singular, so lo: comprarlo.

builds.meaning: I don't know her very well.
I want to see her tonight.

builds.text: Esperamos a Juan en la estación.
builds.meaning: We're waiting for Juan at the station.

builds.text: Te llamo mañana por la tarde.
